title: Your UI is a render tree 🌳

slides.say: React models your app as a tree of components, called the render tree.
The root is your root component, here App. It is the first thing React renders.

steps.say: Each arrow points from a parent to a child it renders. App renders Header and Feed.
Feed renders a Post, and Post renders a Like button. Like button has no children: it is a leaf.

slides.text: Only components appear. No div or h1.
Top-level components affect the speed of everything below. Leaf components often re-render a lot.
slides.say: Why care? Components near the top affect the rendering performance of everything below them. Leaves are often re-rendered frequently.

slides.text: With conditions, the tree can change from one render to the next.
slides.say: And with conditional rendering, the tree can look different from one render to the next.
